identity.title: LipReg4 deletion blocks hypertension induced by gut S. aureofaciens Tu117.

content.abstract: Streptomyces aureofaciens (S. aureofaciens) Tu117 and its metabolite alpha-lipomycin have been implicated in high-salt-induced hypertension. Previous studies showed that high-salt intake increases gut Tu117 abundance and circulating alpha-lipomycin levels. Mechanistically, alpha-lipomycin acts as a TRPV4 antagonist, impairing nitric oxide (NO)- and endothelium-derived hyperpolarizing factor (EDHF)- mediated endothelium-dependent vasodilation and thereby promoting vascular dysfunction and blood pressure (BP) elevation. However, whether hypertension is driven by Tu117 itself or specifically by alpha-lipomycin production remains unclear. Here, we generated a LipReg4 deletion mutant strain (DeltaTu117) using Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 genome editing to selectively abolish alpha-lipomycin biosynthesis. Deletion of LipReg4 did not markedly affect bacterial growth but completely abolished alpha-lipomycin production. Compared with Tu117, DeltaTu117 failed to increase circulating alpha-lipomycin levels or induce a sustained elevation in BP. These findings identify alpha-lipomycin as the key metabolite mediating Tu117-induced hypertension. They further support a direct role of gut microbial metabolites in host BP regulation.
